title: Check: Pods
description: Five questions on the smallest deployable unit and what containers in a Pod share.

questions.prompt: What do containers in the same Pod share? Choose all that apply.

options.text: A network namespace, so they reach each other on localhost
The same lifecycle - they are scheduled together

questions.explanation: Containers in a Pod share the network namespace and any volumes, and are always scheduled onto one node together. Each keeps its own filesystem root from its own image.

questions.prompt: What is distinctive about an init container?

options.text: It runs alongside the app containers
It runs to completion before the app containers start
It restarts whenever the Pod restarts

questions.explanation: Init containers run in order, each to completion, before any app container starts. That is what makes them right for waiting on a dependency or preparing a volume.

questions.prompt: A Pod's `restartPolicy` is `Always`. Which controller would that be wrong for?
questions.explanation: A Job runs Pods to completion, so `Always` would restart a container that finished successfully. Jobs use `OnFailure` or `Never`.

questions.prompt: A Pod named web has two containers. Write the command that shows the logs of the container named sidecar.
questions.explanation: With more than one container, `kubectl logs` needs `-c` to know which one you mean.

questions.prompt: A Pod is stuck in Pending. Where does the lesson tell you to look first?
questions.explanation: Pending means it was never scheduled, so there are no container logs yet. The scheduler explains itself in the events.
